usageSteps: Search for a city, airport, or landmark, or tap "Use my location" to check conditions right where you are.
Review live wind speed, wind gusts, and visibility — key factors for whether it's safe to fly your specific drone model.
Check the planetary Kp index to see whether geomagnetic activity might affect your GPS lock or compass heading.
In the US, see the FAA UAS Facility Map altitude ceiling for the area — then confirm authorization through LAANC or FAADroneZone before you fly.

faq.question: Is FlyDroneMap a substitute for FAA flight authorization?
faq.answer: No. The airspace ceiling shown here comes from the FAA's public UAS Facility Map data and is for planning reference only. You must still obtain authorization through LAANC or FAADroneZone where required before flying.

faq.question: Where does the weather data come from?
faq.answer: Wind speed, gusts, visibility, and temperature come from Open-Meteo's public weather API, updated frequently throughout the day.

faq.question: What is the Kp index and why does it matter for drone flights?
faq.answer: The planetary Kp index measures geomagnetic activity. During elevated Kp levels (geomagnetic storms), GPS positioning accuracy and compass readings can be less reliable, which matters for drones that rely on GPS-hold or return-to-home.

faq.question: Does FlyDroneMap work outside the United States?
faq.answer: Wind, visibility, and Kp index data work worldwide. The FAA airspace ceiling feature is US-specific, since it's sourced from FAA data — outside the US it will show no data for that card.

faq.question: Do I need to create an account?
faq.answer: No. FlyDroneMap works without sign-up — just search a location and check the conditions.

faq.question: Is FlyDroneMap free to use?
faq.answer: Yes, completely free. The site is supported by ads and occasional affiliate links, which never affect the accuracy of the data shown.

sections.heading: Overview
body: FlyDroneMap ("we", "us", "our") operates this website (the "Service"). This Privacy Policy explains what information is collected when you use the Service and how it is used.

sections.heading: Location Data
body: When you search for a location or use the "Use my location" button, the coordinates are sent to our server, which queries third-party weather, geomagnetic, and airspace data providers on your behalf and returns the result to your browser. We do not store your searched locations or associate them with any identifier.

sections.heading: Cookies and Advertising
body: We use Google AdSense to display advertising on the Service. Google and its partners may use cookies, device identifiers, and similar technologies to serve ads based on your prior visits to this and other websites. You can learn more on Google's Ads Privacy page, and opt out of personalized advertising through Google Ads Settings.
We may also use cookies or similar technologies through analytics providers to understand, in aggregate and non-identifying form, how visitors use the Service.

sections.heading: Description of Service
body: FlyDroneMap provides free wind, visibility, and planetary Kp index data, plus a US-specific FAA UAS Facility Map altitude reference, to help with drone flight planning. Data is sourced from third-party public APIs and is provided for informational purposes only.

sections.heading: Not a Flight Authorization
body: Nothing on this Service constitutes, replaces, or guarantees any flight authorization required by the FAA or any other aviation authority. Airspace ceiling information is based on the FAA's public UAS Facility Map dataset and is informational only. You are solely responsible for obtaining any required authorization (such as through LAANC or FAADroneZone) and for complying with all applicable aviation regulations before every flight.

sections.heading: What is FlyDroneMap
body: FlyDroneMap is a free, no-signup dashboard for drone pilots. Search any location to see live wind speed, wind gusts, visibility, and the latest planetary Kp index, plus — for US locations — the FAA's public UAS Facility Map altitude ceiling.

sections.heading: Why We Built It
body: Checking flight conditions usually means piecing together several different apps and government sites. FlyDroneMap brings the numbers that actually matter for a go/no-go decision — wind, gusts, visibility, and geomagnetic activity — into one place, in your language.

sections.heading: Not a Substitute for Official Authorization
body: FlyDroneMap is a planning reference, not a flight authorization tool. Always confirm your flight through LAANC or FAADroneZone (in the US) or your local aviation authority before flying.

sections.heading: Contact
body: Questions or feedback? Reach us at skysmoga@gmail.com.

body: FlyDroneMap participates in affiliate advertising programs, including the Amazon Associates Program and the Coupang Partners Program, designed to provide a means for sites to earn advertising fees by linking to Amazon.com, Coupang.com, and their affiliated sites.

sections.heading: How This Works
body: When you click a product link on FlyDroneMap (for example, a link to a recommended drone accessory) and go on to make a qualifying purchase, we may earn a small commission. This comes at no additional cost to you.

sections.heading: Our Editorial Independence
body: Affiliate relationships never influence the weather, Kp index, or airspace data shown on this Service, which is sourced directly from independent third-party providers.

us.name: United States
summary: Recreational flyers must pass the online TRUST safety test, while commercial drone operations require an FAA Part 107 Remote Pilot Certificate.
Most drones must be registered with the FAA, and flying in controlled airspace near airports requires prior approval through LAANC (Low Altitude Authorization and Notification Capability).
Always check airspace with the B4UFLY app or the FAA's UAS facility map before you fly.

kr.name: South Korea
kr.authority: Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport (MOLIT) · Drone OneStop
summary: Depending on weight and purpose, you must register your drone and obtain flight/aerial-photography approval in advance through the Drone OneStop portal.
Flying without prior approval in no-fly zones, control zones, or restricted zones can result in fines of up to KRW 1.5 million. Most of central Seoul falls under restricted airspace.
On this site, selecting a location in South Korea also shows no-fly zones, control zones, and other airspace layers in color on the map.

jp.name: Japan
jp.authority: Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (MLIT)
summary: Drones weighing 100g or more must be registered with MLIT (including Remote ID); flying an unregistered drone is punishable by law.

Flying near airports, above 150m, over densely inhabited districts (DID), or in emergency-use airspace requires prior permission from the regional civil aviation bureau, applied for online via DIPS2.0.

Night flights, beyond-visual-line-of-sight flights and similar also require separate approval (with some exceptions for certified aircraft/pilots). Always check the latest rules on the official site before flying.

es.name: Spain
summary: Spain follows the EU-wide EASA framework, which splits drone operations into three risk-based categories — Open, Specific, and Certified. Most hobby flying falls under the Open category.
Drone operators must register with AESA and display their registration number on the aircraft.
Where you can fly is defined by AESA's 'UAS geographical zones' service — always check it for restricted areas before flying.
